contract: Tenant-owned, versioned artifact references in the ready Store whose bytes live in the ready integration/object-store Piece: stage, commit, abort, put, new_version, head, get, list, versions, delete, reap and status. One Store stream artifact/<tenant>/<artifact_id> of self-contained non_state_bearing records — artifact_staged, artifact_committed and artifact_deleted each carry the full version record plus resulting state/state_at, with no inference of complete history from surviving rows — under head-revision CAS, plus a best-effort tenant index stream artifact-index/<tenant>. Content hash is SHA-256 over <<hash_format::8, bytes>>, the declared positive format stamped per record and used for verification on every get; a format change is a declared migration. Object keys are artifacts/<tenant>/<artifact_id>/v<version>/<sha256>; tenant and artifact_id are validated to a safe segment before key construction. Every operation presents caller %{tenant, principal, scopes} as consumer-vouched attribution: read paths enforce the recorded access terms and access_expires_at_unix_ms (a hash never grants access), versions filters each returned record by its own terms after the head gate, mutating operations require caller.tenant == record.tenant which the tenant-scoped stream makes structural (plus the recorded terms for delete), and cross-tenant lookup returns :not_found. Appending to an artifact with a committed head enforces that head's recorded terms and access_expires_at_unix_ms: new_version checks before staging and commit re-checks before every staging-to-committed transition, so a denied caller cannot append a head through put, new_version or manual stage+commit; with no committed head appends follow the tenant rule and the first commit establishes the face, and a caller who passes the head's terms may declare the new version's access (narrowing or widening is their declaration). Artifact and index streams require low_water == 0 and validated sequence coverage through the sampled committed Store revision; any retained prefix, missing or malformed row, inconsistent version or illegal transition fails closed as {:store_damaged, info} before object reads, uploads or Store writes. Self-contained rows and contiguous version numbers do not establish complete history after retention. stage reserves the largest encoded lifecycle payload, including the maximum valid state_at timestamp width, before upload. commit verifies object presence, stored transport checksum and size through reconcile_put before the Store write; an unknown put persists an upload: :uncertain staging record resolved by verification, never blind re-put; a Store {:conflict, _} is {:commit_failed, %{expected, observed}} and an indeterminate write is {:commit_failed, :indeterminate}. Object deletes on abort/delete/reap are best-effort with reported outcomes; every already-deleted version's bytes are deletion-attempted again under reap's cleanup result, so a refused/unknown delete is retried by the next reap; list propagates storage and damage failures as errors, never a partial page; reap is caller-driven. Creation, access-expiry and retention fields use the published created_at_unix_ms, access_expires_at_unix_ms and retain_until_unix_ms names in input, public records and persisted JSON.
limits: No atomic object-store plus Store commit: the two boundaries are separate and staged/orphan states are the honest answer, exposed through status (record state plus observed object evidence) and reported object outcomes on abort/delete/reap; bytes may outlive a deleted record until the best-effort delete lands, and every :deleted version's bytes are deletion-attempted again under reap's cleanup result so a refused/unknown delete is retried by the next reap (:absent/:deleted confirms, :refused/:unknown stays pending). A put retry after a lost commit CAS may leave the earlier version staged while a later version commits; status/abort/reap expose and reconcile that permitted non-atomic lifecycle.

The tenant index is a separate stream appended best-effort with no cross-stream transaction: list can miss or lag a just-committed artifact, deduplicates repeated index entries, and is an offset-paginated enumeration of committed heads the caller may access (denied, expired, staging and fully deleted artifacts are omitted). list propagates any index or per-artifact storage/damage failure as an error — a storage failure never returns a successful partial page.

Single-shot upload only through integration/object-store: max_bytes <= min(16 MiB, object_store.max_object_bytes) by default and bounded by construction; no multipart, resumable or streaming upload, no presigned-URL issuance or lifecycle, no malware scanning, no encryption-at-rest policy beyond the provider, no replication, no public sharing.

caller is attribution, not authentication: a richer authorization policy is the consumer's (domain/authorization is deliberately not a dependency); access terms are the durable final check on recorded records only.

hash_format is a declared positive integer 1..255 stamped per record; v1 canonical form is the raw bytes. Verification uses the record's stored format; a genuinely different canonical encoding is a new Piece revision, not a construction option, and no format may be silently reinterpreted.

media_type is a bounded opaque tag (UTF-8 without NUL, 1..256 bytes, default application/octet-stream); metadata is JSON-encodable and bounded by max_metadata_bytes (default 4_096) encoded size plus the Store record bound. stage reserves the largest lifecycle encoding across states and upload outcomes with the maximum valid signed-bigint state_at timestamp, before upload; timestamps are nonnegative signed-bigint Unix milliseconds.

Selected laws cover the access-decision and state-transition tables over ordering outcomes; the production integer comparison (the builtin <) is finite-test-grounded, not proved, the same scoped claim as state/lease.

Access is evaluated on each record's own recorded terms: reads gate on the target version (versions on the head's, or the latest record's when nothing is committed, then per-version), delete adds the recorded terms to the tenant match, and appends to an artifact with a committed head must pass that head's terms and access_expires_at_unix_ms (new_version early, commit before every staging-to-committed transition; no committed head means the tenant rule until the first commit establishes the face). staging records older than staging_ttl_ms are :staging_expired on commit and due for reap.

Self-contained artifact rows do not establish complete history after retention: a highest version or a lifecycle transition can disappear without a gap in version numbers. Artifact and index streams must retain all rows (low_water == 0); any retained prefix fails closed as {:store_damaged, :incomplete_prefix}. Every sequence through the sampled Store revision must be present, ordered and validated, including foreign rows; malformed replies/rows, missing middle or tail positions, inconsistent versions and illegal transitions fail closed before object reads, uploads or Store writes. No artifact-specific history checkpoint or retention recovery is supplied.

reap is caller-driven only with no background process; expiry and retention move records to :deleted and delete bytes best-effort, and every already-:deleted version's bytes are deletion-attempted again under the result's cleanup map so refused/unknown deletes are retried by the next reap. Every entry point refuses inside the caller's open Ecto transaction on the Store's Repo ({:error, :caller_transaction}).

The Piece stores no credential material and reads no environment variable; the object-store credential remains its injected per-call Need. Artifact bytes are returned only by a successful get; record values, errors and events contain no byte payload.

No durability claim beyond the upstream contracts: PostgreSQL durability/fsync and MinIO semantics are the providers'; the Memory double is volatile test evidence only; finite named scenarios on the ready PostgreSQL Store, disposable MinIO and loopback doubles, not unbounded properties.

telemetry.contract: Declared family [:elzoo, :artifact, staged | committed | deleted | integrity_failure] through :telemetry.execute/3 with bounded measurements (size_bytes, version) and metadata (tenant, artifact_id, upload/cause/object/via atoms); no bytes, object keys, credentials or checksums in events. The ready runtime/telemetry schema is closed to the two assembly adapters, so this Piece declares its own family rather than editing a ready Piece (recorded on issue #179).

config.contract: Construction-time Store term, object-store binding, clock and bounds (max_bytes, max_metadata_bytes, staging_ttl_ms, hash_format, object_opts) plus per-call caller/input/options; a change is a new construction value, no hot reconfiguration.

control.contract: commit, abort, delete and reap are recorded durable state transitions with applied ({:ok, record}/{:ok, result}), refused (:not_found/:access_denied/:expired/:deleted/{:invalid, _}/{:invalid, :state}), failed ({:commit_failed, _}/typed object-store outcomes) and indeterminate ({:commit_failed, :indeterminate}) results; delete is idempotent-refused on :deleted; no pause or drain claims, no background reaper.

grounding.claim: A1: an absent principal is denied under every scope presence and expiry ordering, quantified over both; checked by the pinned Cure.
A2: unsatisfied scopes are denied under every expiry ordering, quantified over the ordering; checked by the pinned Cure.
A3: once the recorded terms pass, the decision is the expiry table's answer, quantified over the ordering; checked by the pinned Cure.
A4: a live expiry ordering permits; checked by the pinned Cure.
A5: expiry at the stamp expires; checked by the pinned Cure.
A6: expiry past the stamp expires; checked by the pinned Cure.
T1: staging plus commit yields committed; checked by the pinned Cure.
T2: staging plus abort yields deleted; checked by the pinned Cure.
T3: staging plus delete refuses invalid; checked by the pinned Cure.
T4: staging plus reap yields deleted; checked by the pinned Cure.
T5: committed plus commit stays committed (idempotent); checked by the pinned Cure.
T6: committed plus delete yields deleted; checked by the pinned Cure.
T7: committed plus reap yields deleted; checked by the pinned Cure.
T8: committed plus abort refuses invalid; checked by the pinned Cure.
T9: deleted is terminal for every event, quantified over the event; checked by the pinned Cure.

The pinned Cure compiles and audits the production source (no axioms, holes, unresolved, unaudited, opaque or not-proven-total symbols; zero absurd); four negative controls (PermitExpired, DeniedTermsPermit, StagingDeletePermits, FalseTransition) are rejected at the reflexive line of the named law in the bundled test.

Memory double, disposable MinIO (ELZOO_TEST_S3_*, fail closed), a programmable in-memory S3 double (FakeS3) and loopback stubs: 37 scenarios A1-A3 and L1-L34: A1-A3 (construction, every entry point refuses malformed caller/segment/version input before Store or object effects, bounds), L1-L2 (put/head/get/versions, new_version), L3 (cross-tenant :not_found), L4 (recorded terms deny principal and scope; a hash never grants access), L5 (:expired on head/get/versions/status, delete refused, list filtered), L6 (tampered bytes integrity_mismatch, never served), L7 (absent object evidence refuses commit), L8 (unknown put persists uncertain staging, status exposes it, no blind re-put), L9 (staging_expired), L10-L12 (abort, delete, reaped retention and expired access), L13 (tenant-scoped bounded list omits denied and expired heads, with positive visible controls), L14 (hash_format migration verifies old records under stored format), L15 (no credential or byte payload in record values; nonempty __DIR__-anchored production-source audit for environment reads, also run in the copied consumer), L16-L17 (declared telemetry events), L18 (15 laws compile, audit clean, four negative controls rejected), L19 (finite agreement with the pure tables), L20-L21 (new_version/commit enforce the committed head's recorded terms and expiry; manual stage+commit cannot bypass; version numbers never reused), L22 (versions filters each record by its own terms — denied versions omitted entirely), L23 (self-contained rows persist their fields; prefix, fully retained and retained highest-version histories refuse every operation as {:store_damaged, :incomplete_prefix} before object effects or writes), L24 (an unreadable persisted row fails closed as {:store_damaged, %{first: {:unreadable, _}}} on reads, staging and version allocation), L25 (refused/unknown object deletes are retried by reap's cleanup sweep and reported per version), L26-L28 (list propagates damaged artifact streams, damaged index rows and store unavailability as errors — never a partial page), L29 (missing deletion row, nil sequence, non-map row, duplicate/reordered sequence, wrong-stream row and truncated tail all refuse every operation before object effects or writes), L30 (4095-byte stage and timestamp-width boundary refused without upload/row; admitted boundary commits at growing and maximum timestamp widths), L31 (published timestamp keys persist and decode exactly, missing keys rejected, exact expiry/retention exercised), L32 (commit-time :object_mismatch leaves staging unchanged), L33 (deterministic real Memory CAS conflict preserves the staged row and admits a fresh retry), L34 (paged sequence coverage, concurrent append beyond the sampled revision, foreign index-kind tolerance and second-page damage refusal); finite scenarios.

Ready PostgreSQL Store (ELZOO_TEST_DATABASE_URL, fail closed): P1 durable lifecycle, P2 foreign-row tolerance plus deterministic real CAS conflict from a competing Store append between load and commit, unchanged staging after the losing CAS, and successful fresh retry, P3 staged/committed records are ordinary validated Store rows, P4 caller-transaction refusal; finite scenarios.

Relies on the pinned Cure compiler/kernel for the selected equality laws and the reducible decision/transition tables; the builtin integer comparison is opaque to the kernel, hence ordering outcomes are the proved surface and the comparison is finite-test-grounded.
Jason 1.4.5 encodes and decodes the record payloads (the ready integration/json recipe's direct use); decoding failures are unreadable records.
Ecto SQL 3.14.0 Repo transaction visibility and in_transaction?/0 behind the ready Store's caller-transaction refusal are upstream contracts.
PostgreSQL durability, commit atomicity and visibility reached through the ready Store/Postgrex 0.22.4 are upstream server contracts, not local proofs.
S3 signing and checksum echo through req_s3 0.2.5 under the ready object-store Adapter are upstream contracts; the Adapter's finite result table is its own Contract.
HTTP transport, deadlines and retries through Req 0.7.5 under the ready object-store Adapter are upstream contracts.
telemetry 1.4.2 execute/3 synchronous handler dispatch is the upstream contract; a failed or absent handler never changes an operation result.
Elixir validation, exceptions and BEAM execution are upstream contracts, not proved here.
OTP 29.1.2 GenServer and :crypto SHA-256 are upstream contracts; no exactly-once or disk durability guarantee.

The consumer merges Elzoo.Artifact.kinds/0 into its fold, keeps schema_version 1 in fold.versions and never writes those kinds itself; artifact object keys are written only through this Piece or Elzoo.ObjectStore under its naming; the object-store credential Need stays the consumer's injected binding and is never stored by this Piece; presented callers are consumer-vouched attribution. Artifact and tenant index streams are not pruned; a generic Store checkpoint does not reconstruct artifact lifecycle history.
